Cache.description: A key-value cache served to the project's peers, with a lifetime on every entry. Not a system of record: losing an entry costs a recomputation, never a fact.

description.description: Free-form, human-readable description of this resource.
description.title: Description

tags.description: Arbitrary labels for organizing and filtering this resource.

instances/admission.description: How a new instance is let in. validator: a function decides.
instances/admission.title: Admission

instances/validator/namespace.description: Where that function lives. Omitted means this resource's own scope, then its parents.
instances/validator/namespace.title: Validator Namespace

instances/validator/name.description: A function called before an instance is opened or created: it decides whether that instance may exist, and returns the parameters it gets.
instances/validator/name.title: Validator

limit.description: The most instances this may hold at once. 0 means no ceiling — which is a choice, not a default, so it has to be written.
limit.title: Limit

size.description: Maximum size, as a human string (e.g. "32MB").
size.title: Size

ttl.description: Entry lifetime. A floor, not a guarantee: peers may disagree about existence for up to the clock skew.
ttl.title: Time-To-Live

replicated.description: Whether every peer keeps its own copy of this cache. Omitted means the data lives on one node and other peers reach it over the network. Only a question under raft consensus: crdt and gossip both put a copy on every peer.
replicated.title: Replicated

consensus.description: What happens to concurrent writes to one key. raft: one holder at a time, so a write costs a round trip and nothing is silently discarded. crdt: every node takes the write the moment it arrives and the writes merge last-writer-wins, with nothing refused and nothing waited for. gossip: the write is taken locally and spread best-effort, so an entry may fail to arrive or be dropped — cheapest, and fine where losing one costs a recomputation.
consensus.title: Consensus

namespace.description: Where that secret lives. Omitted means this resource's own scope, then its parents.
namespace.title: Namespace

name.description: Secret holding the key entries are encrypted with, as "secret/<name>".
name.title: Encryption Key

regions/policy.description: pinned: these regions only — the data-residency line. cdn: seeded here, then follows demand within the allowance. failover: exactly two, the first one main. Omit the block for anywhere the allowance permits.
regions/policy.title: Placement

regions/in.description: pinned: every region this is kept in. cdn: the regions it starts in before demand moves it — omit them and the platform seeds the choice.
regions/in.title: Regions

kv/engine.description: Which engine backs it: distributed. distributed is tau's own, replicated across the swarm; the rest are external servers reached over the network.
kv/engine.title: Engine

size.description: Maximum on-disk size, as a human string (e.g. "1GB").
size.title: Size

consensus.description: What happens to concurrent writes to one key. crdt: every node takes a write the moment it arrives and the writes merge last-writer-wins, with nothing refused and nothing waited for. raft: one holder at a time, so a write costs a round trip and nothing is silently discarded.
consensus.title: Consensus

consensus.description: What happens to concurrent writes. raft: one holder at a time, so a write costs a round trip, there is one total order, and nothing is silently discarded. crdt: every node takes the write the moment it arrives and they merge, with nothing refused and nothing waited for — the order converges rather than being decided.
consensus.title: Consensus

visibility_timeout.description: How long a claimed item stays invisible before it becomes deliverable again.
visibility_timeout.title: Visibility Timeout

delay.description: How long an item waits before it becomes deliverable at all, as a human string (e.g. "30s"). Absent means immediately.
delay.title: Delay

max_attempts.description: Deliveries before the item moves to the dead-letter queue.
max_attempts.title: Max Attempts

interval.description: Delay before a failed delivery becomes deliverable again. Absent means the visibility timeout alone governs.
interval.title: Retry Interval

factor.description: Multiplier applied to the interval per further attempt: the delay for attempt n is interval times factor^(n-1), capped by the ceiling. Absent or 1 means a fixed interval.
factor.title: Retry Factor

ceiling.description: The delay never grows past this. Absent means it is not capped.
ceiling.title: Retry Ceiling

namespace.description: Where that queue lives. Omitted means this queue's own scope, then its parents.
namespace.title: Dead Letter Namespace

name.description: Queue that receives items which exhausted max-attempts.
name.title: Dead Letter Queue

consensus.description: What happens to concurrent writes. raft: one holder at a time, so a write costs a round trip, there is one total order, and nothing is silently discarded. crdt: every node takes the write the moment it arrives and they merge, with nothing refused and nothing waited for — the order converges rather than being decided.
consensus.title: Consensus

age.description: How long a record is kept, as a human string (e.g. "168h"). Absent means forever.
age.title: Retention Age

size.description: How much the log keeps before the oldest records are dropped, as a human string (e.g. "1GB"). Absent means it is not capped.
size.title: Retention Size

regions/policy.description: pinned: these regions only — the data-residency line. cdn: seeded here, then follows demand within the allowance. failover: exactly two, the first one main. Omit the block for anywhere the allowance permits.
regions/policy.title: Placement

regions/in.description: pinned: every region this is kept in. cdn: the regions it starts in before demand moves it — omit them and the platform seeds the choice.
regions/in.title: Regions

Workflow.description: An ordered pipeline of functions with retries. Each step runs as its own queue; nothing new has to be deployed to serve it. There is no run state to inspect yet.

id.description: Content-addressed identifier (CID) of this resource. Stable across renames.

timeout.description: Ceiling on one whole run, as a human string (e.g. "1h"). Absent means a run may take as long as its steps do.
timeout.title: Timeout

concurrency.description: How many runs may be in flight at once. Absent means unlimited.
concurrency.title: Concurrency

start.description: The step a start lands on.
start.title: Start

regions/policy.description: pinned: these regions only — the data-residency line. cdn: seeded here, then follows demand within the allowance. failover: exactly two, the first one main. Omit the block for anywhere the allowance permits.
regions/policy.title: Placement

regions/in.description: pinned: every region this is kept in. cdn: the regions it starts in before demand moves it — omit them and the platform seeds the choice.

items.description: One step: what it does, how often it is attempted and how those attempts are spaced, and where failure goes.

name.description: What this step is called. Another step's on-error names it, the queue it becomes is named after it, and a start names one.

namespace.title: Namespace

input.description: What the function is handed, as an expression over the run's state, e.g. "order.lines". Omitted hands it the whole state.
input.title: Input

result.description: Where the function's answer is kept in the run's state, by name. Omitted means the answer replaces the state.
result.title: Result

wait.description: Pause for this long, then carry on: a human string (e.g. "30s", "1h"). A step waits or calls, never both.
wait.title: Wait

attempts.description: How many times this step is run before it has failed. 1 means no retry.
attempts.title: Attempts

interval.description: Delay before a failed attempt is redelivered, e.g. "5s". Omitted means the queue's visibility timeout alone governs.
interval.title: Backoff Interval

factor.description: Multiplier applied to the interval per further attempt. Omitted or 1 means a fixed interval.
factor.title: Backoff Factor

ceiling.description: The delay never grows past this, e.g. "5m". Omitted means no ceiling.
ceiling.title: Backoff Ceiling

on_error.description: Another step to run when this one has exhausted its attempts. The default sends the run to the {workflow}_failed queue, where a person picks it up.
on_error.title: On Error

description: The v2 DSL and its constraints. A resource is one flat document at <kind>/<name>.yaml; a scope is a directory — namespace/<name>/meta.yaml beside that scope's own <kind>/ dirs, nesting as deep as it goes. This schema models the project AS WRITTEN: compiling lowers, so the object that runs holds resources no document here describes. x-tau-ref / x-tau-validation mark checks the compiler enforces that a plain JSON Schema validator cannot.
